complete_extent_checked.section_I: All three addresses, including the target adjective electam after vineam, and all three complete six-part Greek-and-Latin Trisagia.
complete_extent_checked.section_II: All nine reproaches and nine complete Popule meus responses in their printed order.
complete_extent_checked.section_III: Both complete occurrences of Crucem tuam and the complete Psalm 66:2 verse, with the split choir roles.
complete_extent_checked.section_IV: Complete Crux fidelis/Dulce lignum opening antiphon, all nine narrative hymn stanzas from Pange lingua through Sola digna, the Sempiterna doxology with Amen, and all ten alternating half-refrain responses.
complete_extent_checked.functional_text: Opening choir-number explanation, Roman section numbers, numerical choir labels, Antiphon/Psalm/Hymn labels, inline V. marker, and mandatory-conclusion instruction.

semantic_checks: Second-person address and first-person reproach agency, contrasted actions, direct objects, and refrain repetitions agree throughout.

Hymn stanza agents and syntax checked: Factor grieving at the first parent’s deception; divine craft outwitting the betrayer’s craft; Natus sent from the Father; Virgin Mother binding the infant; free self-giving to the Passion; blood and water washing creation.

Crux fidelis and Dulce lignum preserve the noble tree, leaf/flower/fruit comparison, sweet wood, nails, and borne weight. The English is a plain study rendering and makes no claim of reproducing a historical English hymn.
Flecte ramos preserves the address to the tree, branches and taut fibers, natural stiffness softening, and the heavenly King’s limbs upon a gentle trunk.
Sola digna preserves the Cross as bearer of the world’s victim, ark and harbor for the shipwrecked world, and object of anointing by blood poured from the Lamb’s body.
Trinitarian doxology preserves eternal glory, equal glory of Father and Son, equal honor of the Paraclete, and praise of the One and Three.
